messages:
maya: Quick report: Tempest customer LoRA merge + int4 quant produced odd token splitting in SKU extraction tests. Looks like special-token ordering changed between finetune tokenizer and base.

devin: Any short reproducible example?

maya: Run: `python eval_pack/run_eval.py --pack tempest_sku_120 --model merged_tempest_lora --quant int4`

maya: Minimal: INPUT: "SKU: TST-001
Desc: widget"
FP16: "SKU: TST-001"
INT4: "SKU: <unk>-001"
Token diff: hyphen token id moved from 45 -> 48 after merge.

sam: That smells like a tokenizer special-token reorder or different spm build. Two options: (1) remap LoRA embeddings by token id, (2) retokenize & retrain LoRA. Remap is less customer-impacting.

maya: I ran `tools/tokenmap/rebase_lora.py --in lora_tempest.pt --map spm_old_to_new.json --out lora_tempest_rebased.pt`. Can @eval-bot queue a quick pack comparing fp16, int4_raw, int4_rebased based on staging?

eval-bot: queued 5412345685: tempest_sku_120 on merged_tempest fp16,int4_raw,int4_rebased. ETA ~8m. Artifacts will be in /runs/5412345685.

devin: Note: when remapping indices, ensure we also update any quant-block metadata since shifting ids can move tokens between quant blocks and change kernel packing.

maya: Good call. I verified rebase updates embedding rows and also patches quant blocks.

eval-bot: run 5412345685 complete: fp16 EM=0.94, int4_raw EM=0.57, int4_rebased EM=0.89. Remap recovers most cases; 6 templates still fail due to custom punctuation variants.

sam: For the remaining failures, try a surface-string fallback: when remap misses, map by spm.encode(surface) against base vocab and log ambiguous mappings. We can also offer a tiny calibration step that fits LoRA deltas for remapped ids using a small validation set.

maya: Proposed action: (1) add tokenizer-fingerprint check in LoRA merge CI and block unless `--allow-remap` supplied, (2) include remap+patch-quant in merge pipeline by default, (3) offer optional `--calibrate` run using a 40-sample adversarial set (we'll add tempest_alias_40.json), (4) add regression assert to tempest_sku_120: EM_drop(fp16 -> int4_rebased_cal) <= 0.05. I'll open the PR with repro details and the adversarial vectors.

devin: Also add a short note for SEs: "confirm tokenizer fingerprint or provide remap.json".

maya: Will do. If anyone wants additional comparisons (retokenize vs remap vs remap+calibrate) I can queue them on staging.

sam: Thanks, nice catch."
